issues.summary: Prices use a typed hex colour, so they ignore the theme and dark mode.

consequences.note: Prices in the typed green fall just short of 4.5:1 on light surfaces and well short in dark mode.

issues.summary: The promo banner's background is an arbitrary hex value instead of a surface role.

consequences.note: The banner keeps its light background in dark mode, under the dark theme's light text.

issues.summary: Stock labels use Tailwind's gray palette, which the theme removes, instead of text-secondary.
The product list's padding (p-7) isn't on the spacing scale.
Recipe titles hard-code Georgia instead of the heading font role.
The promo's bobbing animation has a typed 0.6 s duration instead of a motion role.
The promo strip uses a primitive colour variable instead of a role.

consequences.note: The primitive variable doesn't exist in the generated CSS, so the strip's text falls back to the dark theme's light text.

issues.summary: The promo strip's background is a typed rgb() colour.

consequences.note: The strip's light background stays light in dark mode, under light text.

issues.summary: MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" is gone, so Motion animations (the bobbing promo) keep moving for people who ask for less motion.
The generated theme CSS was edited by hand (radius.md changed), so it no longer matches the design guide.

The light text-secondary colour is too faint on the light surfaces (about 2.3:1; it needs 4.5:1). Because the partner variant uses the same text-secondary, `motif validate` also reports it "In the Partner variant, light mode": the same problem, not a second one.

consequences.note: Every text-secondary text in light mode fails as rendered: captions, units, inactive navigation.

issues.summary: The promo's small print is primary text faded to 40% opacity, so it's unreadable on the banner.
The promo's dismiss button is 20×20 px; phones need 44×44 px (it only passes the 24 px minimum because nothing sits next to it).
Home has three primary buttons side by side, so nothing says what to do first.
A grid of six identical feature cards with emoji says nothing a customer needs.
Emoji used as UI (the fire on the promo, emoji as feature icons) instead of the app's icons.
Gradient text on the promo headline, a tell of generated UI that the design guide doesn't call for.
The product page's buttons say "Submit" and "Click here" instead of what they do.
The product list has no loading state and no empty state.
An unknown product id crashes the page: there's no not-found state.
The product page has no way back to the list.
The Add buttons appear only on hover, so touch and keyboard users can't find them.
Home centres everything and jumps from a giant headline to tiny caption text for its main paragraph.
